title: ai-software-connector/v1 - per-release connector declaration for one software release
description: A sibling file (connector.json) inside a software release directory, deliberately NOT a field of manifest.json: ai-software-manifest/v1 is additionalProperties:false over a fixed key set, so adding connector/transports/userModes/operations keys to the manifest would make all six published recipes unparseable and break the 3.2 judgement that legacy recipes stay byte-identical. This file says how a platform connector drives the release. Logical names only: absolute paths, interpreter executables and secret values stay in platform config.

adapter.description: Which connector adapter drives this release. This is the new axis; the wire form stays in transports below, whose vocabulary is the published ai-software/v1 kind enum.

connectorRuntime.description: Language the connector itself runs in (P3 builds it Python 3.9-compatible). A different thing from interpreterAlias, which is the software body's own interpreter resolved from the recipe and the frozen snapshot.

interpreterAlias.description: Logical interpreter name for the software body, matching capabilities.snapshot.json runtime.interpreter. Null when the body is not a script. No absolute path here.

userModes.description: How a human uses the same software without a workflow run. A desktop-session adapter must keep native-gui.

credentialInjection.description: How a declared `reference:<name>` reaches this body, so no client's flag spelling lives in shared code (D-87: the shape had no home before 3.2 P4a). The connector writes the value into a mode-0600 file in its own credential workspace, passes only the argv slots below (with {file} substituted), and deletes the file in the same call - the value never enters argv, evidence, the call index or the artifact scan.

capability.description: Must equal a name in manifest.capabilities; checked in P2-b so this file cannot widen what a release offers.

credentials.description: Logical credential needs, same vocabulary as permissionRequests.credentials in the published manifest schema.

network.description: D-84: per-operation network reach. dirsearch's scan is 'scoped'; profiles like local-only declare which of these they admit. Absent means 'none'.

attestation.description: D-84: which availability attestation this software's connector answers use. snapshot-only (default) = declared + frozen snapshot + body digest match; native-tools-list = the connector additionally asks tools/list once. The connector never invents a third mode.

sessionGuidance.description: D-84: how a human drives this software side by side with mediated calls.
